messages:
Anna L.: Quick heads-up from the continuous-batching probe run: seeing frequent kernel-selection flips when a long prompt (>=512) and a fast decode-rate tail (>40 tok/s) collide. Patterns look like kernel A -> B -> A within a single request batch.
Samir: ugh, that would explain jitter in tail latency. Any repro traces?
Anna L.: uploaded a short flamegraph and the probe log to the perf dashboard: <https://perf.internal/redwood/probes/2026-03/continuous-batch-181250|probe-181250>. Key snippet below.
Anna L.: ```
# classifier snapshot (used by probe):
buckets:
  short: prompt_len < 96, target_batch_tokens=64, decode_rate_target=30-80
  med: 96 <= prompt_len < 512, target_batch_tokens=128, decode_rate_target=10-40
  long: prompt_len >= 512, target_batch_tokens=256, decode_rate_target=1-15
kv_prefetch_hysteresis: 0.12  # fraction of token-budget before prefetching
kernel_affinity_threshold: 0.25  # switch if kernel perf delta > 25%
```
Marco: hmm kernel_affinity_threshold of 0.25 seems low with mixed workloads. Flips make sense if decoder kernel B suddenly looks faster for tail tokens then falls back. Can you paste the perf counters?
Anna L.: basic counters: median decode-rate med bucket: 22 tok/s, 95th: 52 tok/s; long bucket median 6 tok/s but 99th spikes to 48 tok/s (these spikes occur during "assistant continuation" short bursts).
Priya: that spike is probably from our new KV prefetch path merged in cc7f9a2. We added aggressive prefetch for long prompts, might be interacting with kernel cache warming.
Samir: ok, two hypotheses: (1) prefetch warms KV causing kernel B to be faster temporarily, (2) admission policy mixes opposite decode-rate requests resulting in a pooled batch with conflicting optimal kernels.
Marco: agree. Quick experiment: increase kv_prefetch_hysteresis to 0.25 and bump kernel_affinity_threshold to 0.4 in canary and rerun the probe for 6h. Also add a classifier rule to avoid co-batching long+high-decode short tails.
Anna L.: I can push a canary config: <https://github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/configs...|pr#config-331> (will start at 20:05 UTC).
ci-bot: build passed for pr#331 — integration tests ok.
Samir: add an admission check: if queued batch contains any long prompts and any short prompts with recent decode_rate > 35 tok/s then split the batch (prefer latency SLO). Pseudocode: ```if any(long) and any(short_high): split_to_strata()```
Marco: and record per-batch kernel decision entropy metric (how often kernel flips inside a serving window). If entropy > 0.3, mark batch for trace capture.
Priya: noted regression candidate cc7f9a2 — I'm going to run a targeted microbenchmark to verify kv prefetch impact on kernel timings.
Anna L.: timeline: canary deploy config at 20:05 UTC, capture traces for next 6h. If kernel flips drop > 50% then we keep hysteresis change.
ops-bot: alert-snapshot: canary started (canary/config-331) at 2026-03-17T20:05:12Z.
Marco: I'll own the follow-up analysis and open a small RFC if we need a longer-term scheduler change (microburst-aware admission). Assigning to @Marco.
Samir: thanks — also let's add a short eval to Redwood Optimize to see unit-cost delta with these changes.
Anna L.: will post summary + perf diff tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
Priya: if the microbenchmark confirms, we should consider making the classifier produce a "no-co-batch" tag for long+burst short combos. Low-risk but helps stable kernel affinity.
Anna L.: agreed. capturing action items:
- Marco: analyze traces + open RFC if needed
- Priya: microbenchmark on cc7f9a2 prefetch path
- Samir: add admission split rule to probe harness
- Anna L.: run canary + post perf diff
(end)
